extracted.intended_audience: university research administrators, university fiscal officers, principal investigators, and federal agency/grant auditors responsible for applying OMB Circular A-21
extracted.subtask_short: effort reporting under OMB Circular A-21
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing and documenting distribution of salary/personal-service costs and related allowability rules under the 1982 revision of OMB Circular A-21 for educational institutions, including acceptable methods, definitions of institutional functions, and auditing/verification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Major Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Major functions of an institution refers to instruction, organized research, other sponsored activities, and other institutional activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction includes teaching and training activities (and departmental research and, where agreed, university research). Sponsored instruction/training may be considered a major function even if accounted under instruction. Departmental research (not separately budgeted/organized) is treated as part of instruction, not as a separate major function. Organized research means all research and development activities that are separately budgeted and accounted for and includes sponsored research and research training where such activities utilize the same facilities and are not included elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation for Personal Services — General Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The distribution of salaries and wages (direct or indirect) must be based on payrolls documented in accordance with the generally accepted practices of colleges and universities; institutions may use a residual category for activities not directly charged to sponsored agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes that teaching, research, service, and administration are often inextricably intermingled and that precise assessment is not always feasible; reliance on reasonably accurate approximations is acceptable and a degree of tolerance in measurement is appropriate. There is no single best method for documenting distribution of personal services; methods must meet the criteria specified by the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Acceptable Methods for Apportioning Salaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods used to apportion salaries and wages must meet specific institutional-record and verification criteria to be acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key criteria: (a) the payroll distribution system must be incorporated into the institution's official records, reasonably reflect the activity for which the employee is compensated, and encompass both sponsored and all other activities on an integrated basis; (b) the method must recognize after-the-fact confirmation/determination so costs represent actual costs unless a mutually satisfactory alternative agreement is reached; (c) the payroll system must allow confirmation of activity allocable to each sponsored agreement and each category needed to identify indirect costs and the functions to which they are allocable (components not initially identified may be subsequently distributed by reasonable methods such as suitably conducted surveys, statistical sampling, or negotiated fixed rates); (d) the system may reflect categories as percentage distributions of total activities; (e) estimates used initially must have changes identified and entered into the payroll distribution system when appropriate — short-term fluctuations (one or two months) need not be considered provided distributions are reasonable over a longer term; (f) the system must provide for independent internal evaluations to ensure effectiveness and compliance; (g) where these criteria are met, institutions will not be required to provide additional documentation for the effort actually performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan-Confirmation Method Standards (Example of Acceptable Method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards that a plan-confirmation (budgeted/planned/assigned work activity) system must meet to be acceptable for professorial/professional staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must be incorporated into official records and encompass both sponsored and other activities; reasonably reflect only the activity for which the employee is compensated (incidental work need not be included); reflect activity applicable to each sponsored agreement and categories needed to identify indirect costs (indirect activities may initially be in a residual category and later determined by alternate methods); provide for modification of salary/salary distribution when a significant change in work activity occurs (documented by a responsible official and entered into the system); at least annually a statement will be signed by employee, principal investigator, or responsible official using suitable means of verification that the salaries/wages charged are reasonable in relation to work performed; provide for independent internal evaluation of system integrity; institutions using this method shall not be required to provide additional support/documentation for effort actually performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-the-Fact Activity Records (Example Method)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternative acceptable method where distribution of salaries and wages is supported by activity reports recorded after the work is performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page begins description of this method as an acceptable example (the document prescribes activity-reporting mechanisms to support distribution). (Full prescribed details appear beyond the provided excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee Confirmation Not Required; Suitable Means of Verification Permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirmation of direct and indirect cost activities may be made by responsible persons using suitable means of verification; employee signature is not a required form of confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revision removes 'firsthand knowledge' wording and explicitly states that university officials can confirm distributions using suitable verification. This permits institutions flexibility in who signs/validates effort reports and reduces mandatory employee attestation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a Residual Category and Subsequent Allocation of Indirect Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities may treat all activities not directly charged to sponsored agreements in a residual category whose components need not initially be separately documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components in the residual category may subsequently be distributed to indirect cost pools or departmental expenses by reasonable methods mutually agreed to with the government, including suitably conducted surveys, statistical sampling procedures, application of negotiated fixed rates, or other reasonable means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and Accounting for Significant Changes in Work Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must identify, review, and document significant changes in an employee's distribution of effort and enter those changes into the payroll distribution system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term fluctuations (e.g., one or two months) need not be adjusted as long as distributions are reasonable over a longer-term period (such as an academic period). Significant changes must be documented over the signature of a responsible official and entered into the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Internal Evaluations of Effort-Reporting Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must provide for independent internal evaluations to ensure the system's effectiveness and compliance with Circular A-21 standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such evaluations are required for any payroll distribution system to verify integrity and compliance with the criteria (this is cited both in the general criteria and in the plan-confirmation example).

rubrics_metrics.name: No Additional Documentation Required If System Meets Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If an institution's payroll distribution system meets the Circular's criteria and standards, the institution will not be required to provide additional support or documentation for the effort actually performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit relief provision: meeting the enumerated criteria (integration into official records, after-the-fact confirmation, ability to allocate to sponsored agreements, independent evaluations, etc.) means auditors should not demand more granular timekeeping documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of Interest Costs and Capital Equipment/Building Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest costs are recognized only for interest actually paid to external parties; capital equipment and building coverage thresholds and effective dates are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifications: the Circular intends to recognize interest actually paid to external parties (not imputed interest on endowment/internal funds); the equipment threshold for allowable interest was lowered to $10,000 (from an earlier $25,000); coverage clarified that newly constructed buildings and major reconstruction/remodeling completed after July 1, 1962 are covered. Agencies responded to comments to clarify definitions of 'equipment' and 'capital equipment'.
